wiki-iran.standing: Daily readers of the English Wikipedia article on Iran, a country of some 90 million on the northern shore of the Persian Gulf. It borders the Strait of Hormuz, through which about a fifth of the world's oil passes.
wiki-iran.recent: Trump threatened to 'annihilate' Iran in his UN speech, and talks in New York that week turned to the terms for reopening Hormuz. Iran has since said the strait stays shut until seven conditions are met, the US answered its plan through Qatar, and the foreign ministry confirmed serious debate on quitting the nuclear treaty.

brent.standing: The price of a barrel of light crude from North Sea fields, and the reference against which most of the world's traded oil is priced. Petrol, diesel, freight and jet fuel costs follow it within weeks.
brent.recent: The Iran war shut the Strait of Hormuz and took almost 3 billion barrels off the market, Aramco says. Middle East exports are back above pre-war levels and the G7 pledged a release of stocks, but OPEC+ held November quotas and blasts beside a tanker off Mokha keep buyers paying for the risk of another closure.

wti.standing: West Texas Intermediate, the light, low-sulphur crude delivered by pipeline to Cushing, Oklahoma, and the benchmark American oil is priced against. US petrol and diesel prices follow it.
wti.recent: The war that set an Iranian blockade on the Strait of Hormuz took Gulf barrels off the market, and governments covered the gap by emptying emergency reserves. Middle East exports have since climbed back above pre-war levels, but Saudi Aramco says refilling those stockpiles could take two years, and buyers still pay for the risk of another cut.

natgas-hh.standing: The price of natural gas delivered at Henry Hub, a pipeline junction in Louisiana, and the benchmark for the US market. It moves on weather and storage levels, and American power bills and LNG export contracts are priced off it.
natgas-hh.recent: The fortnight's gas news was about seaborne cargoes rather than the US pipeline market: more Qatari LNG tankers cleared Hormuz, and South Korea said it never pledged $54bn to an Alaska gas project. Neither accounts for the price at Henry Hub.

wheat.standing: The world price of a tonne of wheat, the most widely traded food grain. Importing states from North Africa to South Asia buy against it, so it reaches the cost of bread and the size of government subsidy bills.
wheat.recent: The fortnight's news shows what dearer wheat does rather than what lifted it. A National Assembly committee in Pakistan wants a Rs5,000 per 40kg support price, Egypt delayed a second bread price request in months, and India closed its weakest monsoon since 2015 under a strong El Niño.

rice.standing: The export price of a tonne of Thai 5% broken white rice, the grade world trade is benchmarked on. Half the world eats rice daily and little of the crop crosses a border, so one exporter's ban moves the price fast.
rice.recent: India's monsoon ended 12.6% below the long-term average, its weakest since 2015, while floods killed at least 62 people in Uttar Pradesh and Bangkok had its worst flooding in 15 years. All of that came after the latest monthly reading, so none of it accounts for the price shown.

copper.standing: The price of a tonne of refined copper, set on the London Metal Exchange. The metal goes into wiring, motors and power grids, so it tracks construction and electrification, and the export income of Chile, Peru and Congo rides on it.
copper.recent: China made guarantees of copper supply its condition for approving the Anglo Teck merger, three sources say, a sign of how tightly buyers are guarding access to the metal. Peru's export boom rests on the copper it sells to China. Neither accounts for the long climb in the price, which was under way well before both.

us-10y.standing: The interest rate the US government pays to borrow for ten years. It is the base rate for American mortgages and for dollar borrowing worldwide, so governments and companies everywhere refinance against it.
us-10y.recent: The climb follows the volume of debt Washington sells to cover its deficits, and inflation: traders priced in four Fed rate hikes by June 2027. Japan's 10-year yield neared a 30-year high in the same sell-off, and Trump tied $5,000 checks, estimated above $1 trillion, to the midterms while interest already costs about $1 trillion a year.

sp500.standing: An index of 500 large US-listed companies weighted by market value, covering roughly four-fifths of the American stock market. Pension funds and index trackers worldwide hold it, so its moves reach savers far beyond the US.
sp500.recent: Fed officials questioned JPMorgan, Wells Fargo, Barclays and Morgan Stanley about private credit, and rising bond yields drew attention in Washington to the roughly $1 trillion a year the US pays in interest. Neither accounts for the index's path, whose turning points fall weeks before these stories.

nasdaq100.standing: The 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq exchange in New York, weighted by market value. A handful of technology giants make up most of it, so it moves with what investors will pay for big tech.
nasdaq100.recent: The climb ran through a string of wins for its heaviest members. Nvidia authorized a record $150 billion share buyback, Meta launched a paid AI platform for businesses, a judge dismissed the Chegg and Penske antitrust suits against Google, and Trump signed an accord letting top tech firms self-police AI development.

us-gas-retail.standing: The average price US drivers pay for a gallon of regular gasoline, surveyed at filling stations nationwide. It follows crude oil with a lag, feeds straight into inflation, and is the price American voters watch most closely.
us-gas-retail.recent: The war with Iran squeezed supplies of crude and refined fuels, and the pump price follows crude. About one-third of US states have cut fuel taxes weeks before the 3 November midterms, giving up road-fund revenue to mask a price that tax holidays do not set. The International Energy Agency is releasing 100 million barrels of oil and fuel.

natgas-ttf.standing: The price of gas at the Title Transfer Facility, a Dutch virtual trading hub, and the benchmark for European gas contracts. Power prices and heating bills across the continent follow it, and it sets what Europe bids for LNG.
natgas-ttf.recent: Qatar's LNG leaves through the Strait of Hormuz, which Iran says is shut, and unlike Saudi crude it has no pipeline around it, so the US-Iran war took cargoes that European and Asian buyers compete for off the market. Tankers loaded at Ras Laffan are now reappearing outside the strait, and September shipments were the highest since the war began.

vix.standing: The Cboe Volatility Index, derived from the prices of options on the S&P 500. It measures how large a swing in US stocks traders are paying to insure against over the next 30 days, and it rises when they are afraid.
vix.recent: The strain of late September showed up in bonds rather than here: Treasury volatility jumped from 80 to 104 in 2 days while stocks stayed calm. Nothing else in the fortnight's news accounts for the equity gauge's own drift.

fx-pkr.standing: What one US dollar costs in Pakistani rupees. Pakistan buys its fuel and much of its food in dollars and pays for them with remittances and IMF loans, so the rate sets what petrol, cooking gas and flour cost at home.
fx-pkr.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's news accounts for the rupee's drift. Islamabad raised the petrol price and reviewed its fuel subsidy for motorcycle riders, used-car imports surged after rules were eased, and Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf began its march on Islamabad after talks failed.

fx-ngn.standing: What one US dollar costs in naira, the currency of Africa's most populous country. Nigeria earns most of its dollars from crude oil and imports much of what it consumes, so the rate feeds straight into what things cost.
fx-ngn.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's news accounts for the rate. What it carried was about the institutions behind the currency: auditors found ₦1.63 trillion unaccounted for at Nigeria's central bank, which itself said multiple FX windows cost the country 3% of GDP, and the state oil company lost 77.6% of its fuel-products revenue.

fx-egp.standing: What one US dollar costs in Egyptian pounds, so a rising line is a weaker pound. Egypt imports much of its wheat and fuel, and a weaker pound reaches the price of bread and the cost of servicing its dollar debt.
fx-egp.recent: Nothing reported from Cairo in the past fortnight accounts for the pound's weakening. Egypt delayed a decision on a 2nd bread price hike request in months, postponed its criminal procedures code a year, and arrested all 6 Matsda2sh journalists within two days; none of these is a currency event.

fx-try.standing: How many Turkish lira buy one US dollar. Turkey imports most of its energy and its companies borrow heavily in foreign currency, so a weaker lira feeds straight into inflation and into the cost of repaying those loans.
fx-try.recent: The weeks' news from Turkey was military and diplomatic: a base at Bashiqa passing to Iraqi control, a Russian offer to let it move its S-400s, and a pledge alongside Pakistan to deploy troops to Saudi Arabia. None of it accounts for the exchange rate.

fx-bdt.standing: Bangladesh's currency, priced in taka per US dollar and managed by the central bank inside a narrow band. Garment exports and money sent home by workers abroad earn the dollars that pay for the country's imported fuel and food.
fx-bdt.recent: The news about Bangladesh in these weeks was diplomatic rather than economic: Sheikh Hasina's arrival in India resurfaced through an envoy's account, Dhaka skipped the BRICS summit in Delhi, and it traded pledges of closer ties with Iran. None of it accounts for the exchange rate.

fx-idr.standing: The currency of Indonesia, Southeast Asia's largest economy, quoted as rupiah per US dollar, so a rising line is a weaker rupiah. It moves with coal, palm oil and nickel exports and with foreign demand for its government bonds.
fx-idr.recent: The fortnight's news on Indonesia was a new finance minister facing a test of delivery, questions over the focus of Prabowo's multialignment, and Chinese mining firms rated laggards on sustainability. None of it accounts for the rupiah's move.

fx-lbp.standing: How many Lebanese pounds buy one US dollar. The currency lost nearly all its value in the banking collapse that began in 2019, and the central bank now holds it at a managed rate in an economy that runs largely on dollars.
fx-lbp.recent: The news about Lebanon in these weeks was about security, not money: Israeli minister Smotrich called for annexing parts of the country, and Israel pressed for a US-led force to disarm Hezbollah. None of it accounts for the exchange rate.

fx-cny.standing: China's currency, quoted as the number of yuan one US dollar buys. The central bank sets a daily reference rate and limits trading around it, so the rate reflects policy as much as the market, and prices Chinese exports.
fx-cny.recent: Xi Jinping's three-day visit to Washington fell in the middle of the window, and the summit with Trump wrapped with little changed: the trade war between the two produced no settlement that would have given a managed currency a reason to be reset. Nothing else in the fortnight's news bears on the rate.

fx-inr.standing: How many Indian rupees buy one US dollar, so a rising line is a weaker rupee. India imports most of its oil and pays for it in dollars, and the Reserve Bank of India manages the rate closely by buying and selling reserves.
fx-inr.recent: Indian shares slid over the same weeks: the Sensex in Mumbai extended a seventh week of declines, dropping more than 900 points in one session. New Delhi cut its export duty on diesel to 16 rupees a litre from 20. None of the reporting names a cause for the currency itself.

fx-brl.standing: What one US dollar costs in Brazilian reais, so a falling number means a stronger real. It moves on soy, iron ore and oil exports, on Brazil's high interest rates, and on doubts about how much the government borrows.
fx-brl.recent: The real was at its weakest as the campaign closed in disorder: the final debate was cancelled two days before the vote, and the deposit insurer's $7.7bn payout for Banco Master's collapse hung over the race. It strengthened once the first round was counted, with Flávio Bolsonaro beating Lula 47% to 45.1% and the presidency going to a runoff.

fx-mxn.standing: How many Mexican pesos one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker peso. The most traded emerging-market currency, it moves on US interest rates, trade policy and the remittances workers send home.
fx-mxn.recent: The fortnight's news from Mexico was Hurricane Polo, which grew from tropical storm to Category 5 in 24 hours and made two landfalls on the Pacific coast, and 14 Latin American nations declaring cartels foreign terrorist organizations. None of it accounts for the peso's slide.

fx-eur.standing: How many euros one US dollar buys, the exchange rate between the world's two most used currencies. It moves on the gap between European Central Bank and Federal Reserve interest rates, and on the price of the energy Europe imports.
fx-eur.recent: An energy shock from the Middle East war is running through the euro area: inflation jumped in September, and the European Central Bank has already been raising its rate. Business activity still grew at its fastest pace in nearly three and a half years, while the US pressed Europe to release emergency diesel stocks.

fx-jpy.standing: How many yen one US dollar buys, so a higher number is a weaker yen. Japan's low interest rates make it the currency investors worldwide borrow in, and it sets the cost of the fuel and food Japan imports.
fx-jpy.recent: Cheap Japanese rates have held the yen down, and bonds moved ahead of the central bank: the 10-year yield reached 3.11%, near a 30-year high. Three sources told Reuters the Bank of Japan may say this month that underlying inflation has reached its 2% goal, dropping its own stated reason to hold.

fx-rub.standing: How many rubles buy one US dollar. Russia earns its hard currency from oil and gas, so the rate moves with energy prices, sanctions and capital controls, and it feeds straight into what Russians pay for imported goods.
fx-rub.recent: The ruble firmed as sanctions pressure eased: the EU dropped two Russian tycoons from its list, Trump invited Putin to the Miami G20, and the Kremlin confirmed energy talks with US negotiators. It slipped after Washington floated an 18 October decision on secondary sanctions and Ukraine claimed 51% of Russia's oil refining capacity was out of action.

fx-zar.standing: How many rand one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker rand. Africa's most traded currency, it moves with the gold and platinum South Africa exports and with foreign appetite for its government bonds.
fx-zar.recent: The fortnight brought US visa curbs and travel bans aimed at Pretoria, a rejected A$39bn bid by Gold Fields for Northern Star, and shootings that killed 27 people in Gauteng. None of it accounts for the rand's weakening against the dollar.

btc.standing: A digital currency capped at 21 million coins and run by a network no government or company controls. It sets the tone for the whole crypto market and trades around the clock, every day.
btc.recent: Spot bitcoin ETFs took in nearly $1 billion in a single day at the peak, the 9th largest inflow ever. The slide after it came as traders priced in 4 Fed rate hikes by June 2027, hackers took $350 million from the exchange Bitget and the Clarity Act died in the US Senate. On 2 October the US approved its first 3x leveraged crypto funds.

eth.standing: The native token of the Ethereum blockchain, paid as the fee for every transaction and smart contract run on it. Most stablecoins and decentralised finance settle there, so its price tracks demand for that activity.
eth.recent: US law pulled both ways: the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act died in the Senate, then the US approved its first 3x leveraged crypto funds on 2 October. Hackers took $350 million from the exchange Bitget, and developers are testing Glamsterdam, which more than triples block size. None of it accounts for the price.

paxg.standing: A token issued by Paxos, each one backed by an ounce of gold held in London vaults, so it tracks the spot price of bullion. Gold pays no interest, so it falls when bond yields and the dollar rise; central banks hold it as reserves.
paxg.recent: Treasury yields surged, lifting the return on bonds against a metal that yields nothing, while rising oil prices and a higher US dollar pushed the same way. Separately, Intercontinental Exchange began offering gold futures in London, where physical bars have traded privately between banks rather than on an exchange.

wiki-artificial-intelligence.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on artificial intelligence, the field of building machines that do tasks associated with human thought. It is a rough gauge of how many people are trying to understand the technology.
wiki-artificial-intelligence.recent: Trump named intelligence director Jay Clayton to lead a new task force, and six executives signed a one-page accord with no legal force. The same week OpenAI warned over 100 organisations that its models may have entered their systems, fired two safety researchers and a program manager, and lost its safety-report lead David Robinson.

wiki-russia.standing: How many people open Wikipedia's article on Russia each day. Russia is the world's largest country and a nuclear-armed oil and gas exporter, and a surge marks a day its war, diplomacy or a domestic shock drew in new readers.
wiki-russia.recent: The EU dropped two Russian tycoons from its sanctions list in a renewal deal, angering Ukraine, and Trump invited Putin to the Miami G20 days later. Russia then hit a Kyiv bridge as Merz visited, and a plague-institute technician died in Irkutsk; dozens are quarantined while the health watchdog calls the diagnosis an unconfirmed rumour.

wiki-china.standing: The number of people who open Wikipedia's article on China each day. It is a rough gauge of when the world's second-largest economy has pushed into public curiosity, and it jumps on summits, crises and disasters.
wiki-china.recent: Xi Jinping spent three days in Washington with Trump, a visit that wrapped with little changed beyond $30bn in tariff cuts led by farm goods and holiday decorations. The peak came days later, as Trump denied asking Xi about potential US arms sales, after a US envoy said Beijing had assured Washington it isn't aiding Iran.

wiki-strait-of-hormuz.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow channel between Iran and Oman that carries about a fifth of the world's oil. The count jumps when shipping there comes under threat.
wiki-strait-of-hormuz.recent: Iran offered to reopen the strait, Trump rejected the proposal, and talks in New York turned to reopening terms. Iran now says Hormuz stays shut until 7 conditions are met, and the US answered its 7-day plan through Qatar. UKMTO says 2 tankers were hit in the strait, yet Kpler counts non-Iranian crude flows back at the pre-war level.

wiki-india.standing: How many people open the Wikipedia article on India each day. The count jumps when an election, a disaster, a cricket final or a border clash sends readers looking for background on the world's most populous country.
wiki-india.recent: A fight over voter-roll deletions has filled the streets: police closed 11 metro stations in New Delhi, detained 160 marchers including Prashant Bhushan and Yogendra Yadav, and the chief justice asked who altered Form 6. India also signed 5 pacts with Switzerland as trade talks with Washington stalled. None of it accounts for the earlier peak.

cp:hormuz.standing: One-fifth of global seaborne oil passes through this 21-mile strait between Iran and Oman.
cp:hormuz.recent: Iran says the strait stays shut until 7 conditions are met, and the US answered its 7-day plan through Qatar. Some ships now risk the crossing: more Qatari LNG tankers cleared it over the weekend, an Iraqi state tanker carried 2 million barrels through, and Kuwait, which has no pipeline around it, pumps about 75% of its prewar oil.

cp:bab-el-mandeb.standing: Between Yemen and Djibouti — the Red Sea’s southern gate. Houthi attacks since 2023 have pushed container shipping to reroute around Africa.
cp:bab-el-mandeb.recent: Houthi forces took the Yemeni shore of the strait in September, when government troops fled Mokha, putting launch sites beside the shipping lane. Saudi-backed Yemeni troops now say they have secured Dhubab and cut Houthi roads to the coast, and blasts erupted beside a tanker off Mokha. The summer trough came before any of it.

cp:suez.standing: Egypt’s 120-mile artery carries roughly 12% of global trade. The 2021 closure disrupted supply chains for weeks; Red Sea instability keeps it volatile.
cp:suez.recent: Yemen's army says it secured Dhubab, beside Bab al-Mandab, and retook Mocha, while Saudi Arabia plans an offensive against the Houthis, who say they struck an oil facility near Riyadh. Ships bound for the canal enter the Red Sea through that strait. The fighting came after the canal's thinnest days, which nothing reported accounts for.

cp:malacca.standing: Between Malaysia and Sumatra — the fastest route between the Indian and Pacific Oceans. Over 80,000 ships a year, including most of China’s oil imports.
cp:malacca.recent: The fortnight's shipping news sat upstream of this strait, not in it: Middle East crude exports climbed back above pre-war levels and more Qatari LNG cleared Hormuz, cargoes headed for Asian importers, while blasts erupted beside a tanker off Mokha. None of it reports a disruption in Malacca itself.

cp:taiwan.standing: Between mainland China and Taiwan — roughly 40% of the world’s container traffic passes through, and the flashpoint of any US–China confrontation.
cp:taiwan.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's news touched the shipping itself. Xi's visit to Washington wrapped with little changed, Taiwan received the first 2 of 66 ordered F-16V fighters, and the Philippines says it forced a Chinese survey ship from Batanes. None of it closed a lane or rerouted a vessel.

cp:panama.standing: 50-mile shortcut between the Atlantic and Pacific. Drought in 2023–24 cut daily transits by half — a live example of climate binding to trade.

cp:bosporus.standing: Istanbul’s 20-mile waterway links the Black Sea to the Mediterranean — the only route for Russian naval access and Ukrainian grain exports.
cp:bosporus.recent: Nothing reported over these weeks accounts for the thinner traffic. The one event on this route came after the data ends: a cargo ship caught fire and sank in the Black Sea close to Romania's shore, killing 2 crew, and Ukraine says a Russian drone hit it on the grain corridor that leads here.

cp:gibraltar.standing: 8 miles between Morocco and Spain — the only Atlantic–Mediterranean link. A surveillance chokepoint for Russian submarines and sanctioned oil.
cp:gibraltar.recent: The fortnight's news from the strait's two shores was about people, not ships: 8,300 migrants sat in shelters in Ceuta while 4,000 slept outside, Morocco named El Mansouri its first female prime minister, and Sánchez called a snap election in Spain. None of it touched the shipping lanes or accounts for the traffic.

cp:dover.standing: The busiest shipping lane on Earth — 400+ ships a day squeeze through the English Channel’s 21-mile narrows.

cp:cape-of-good-hope.standing: The 3,000-mile detour around southern Africa — the alternative when the Red Sea is closed. The new default for tankers since Houthi attacks began.
cp:cape-of-good-hope.recent: The fortnight's shipping news sat further north: Iran kept Hormuz shut pending its seven conditions, Middle East crude exports still rose above pre-war levels, and blasts erupted beside a tanker off Mokha, near Bab el-Mandeb. None of it accounts for the traffic rounding the Cape, and the Mokha blasts came after the latest count.

cp:kerch.standing: Between Crimea and Russia — the only access to the Sea of Azov. A flashpoint since 2014 and contested throughout the Russia–Ukraine war.
cp:kerch.recent: Nothing reported in the fortnight accounts for the halt in traffic here. The nearest shipping story was elsewhere in the Black Sea: a cargo ship caught fire and sank close to Romania's shore, 2 crew died and 11 were rescued, and Zelenskyy says a Russian drone hit it.

mkt:tadawul.standing: The Tadawul All Share Index, which tracks every main-market company on the Saudi Exchange in Riyadh. It is the Arab world's largest market by value and Aramco dominates it. It trades Sunday to Thursday, so it opens the global week.
mkt:tadawul.recent: In the window, the main news touching Saudi Arabia was the Houthi advance: they seized a key port and took control of Yemen's Red Sea coast, a vital shipping route. None of it was reported in terms of Saudi-listed companies, and none of it accounts for the index's move.

mkt:bist.standing: The 100 largest companies on Borsa İstanbul, Türkiye's only stock exchange. It is priced in lira, so its level carries the country's inflation as much as its earnings: read the direction, not the number.
mkt:bist.recent: The news about Türkiye in these weeks was military and diplomatic, not economic: Turkey agreed to pass its Bashiqa base to Iraqi control, Moscow said it may let Turkey move its S-400s, and Turkey and Pakistan pledged troops to Saudi Arabia after Houthi drone attacks on Riyadh. None of it accounts for the fall in Istanbul shares.

mkt:dfm.standing: The Dubai Financial Market General Index tracks the shares listed on Dubai's stock exchange, the Gulf's main listing venue for property and banking. It trades Monday to Friday, unlike Riyadh.
mkt:dfm.recent: The fortnight brought the war to Dubai's doorstep. Missiles fell on Gulf cities, the Hormuz closure pushed Emirati trade overland through Oman, the UAE suspended trade with Iran in August, and Algeria cut ties. None of it falls on the dates of the index's high or low, so none of it explains the price.

mkt:bursa-malaysia.standing: The 30 largest companies on Bursa Malaysia, the Kuala Lumpur stock exchange, weighted by market value. The exchange is the world's largest market for Islamic finance instruments and the centre of the global sukuk trade.
mkt:bursa-malaysia.recent: Malaysia's news in the fortnight was the deportation of 1,476 Myanmar detainees on navy ships from Lumut, the death of former first lady Siti Hasmah at 100, and the Mihas 2026 halal showcase in Kuala Lumpur. None of it accounts for the index.

mkt:idx.standing: Every company listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange in Jakarta, weighted by size. It is the market of the world's largest Muslim-majority country, and banks and commodity producers carry most of its weight.
mkt:idx.recent: Nothing published in the past fortnight accounts for the index's path. The news from Indonesia was about a new finance minister facing a test of delivery, and about MSCI rating 80% of Chinese mining firms as laggards on sustainability, neither of which is tied to a move in Jakarta's shares.

mkt:tse.standing: The Nikkei 225 tracks 225 large companies on the Tokyo Stock Exchange, Japan's main market, weighted by share price. Tokyo is Asia's largest exchange, and the first major market to price each trading day.
mkt:tse.recent: Three sources say the Bank of Japan may declare its 2% inflation goal reached, and Japan's 10-year yield hit 3.11%, near a 30-year high, as a global bond sell-off deepened. Both point to dearer borrowing, which normally weighs on shares, and nothing in the fortnight's news accounts for the index's climb.

mkt:hkex.standing: The Hang Seng Index tracks the largest and most traded companies on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. It is where mainland Chinese companies meet foreign capital, and the clearest daily read on sentiment toward China.
mkt:hkex.recent: Xi's three-day visit to Washington ended with little changed: Beijing and the US cut tariffs on $30bn of goods, led by farm goods and holiday decorations, and opened an AI safety channel. Days later the FBI arrested a woman accused of watching the family of Taiwan's president for China. None of it accounts for the index's path.

mkt:sse.standing: The SSE Composite tracks every share listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange, mainland China's main board, weighted by market value. Largely closed to foreign investors, it follows domestic policy more than global risk appetite.
mkt:sse.recent: Xi's three-day visit to Washington wrapped with little changed, and the $30bn in tariff cuts that followed led with farm goods and holiday decorations. Beijing separately demanded copper guarantees before approving the Anglo Teck merger. None of it accounts for the index's fall, which began well before the summit.

mkt:krx.standing: The Korea Composite Stock Price Index: every common share on the main board of the Korea Exchange, South Korea's market in Seoul. Samsung and SK Hynix dominate it, making it a proxy for the global semiconductor cycle.
mkt:krx.recent: The fortnight's news from Seoul was diplomatic rather than financial: a row with Ukraine over the transfer of North Korean prisoners, landmine blasts in the Demilitarized Zone that wounded 3 soldiers, and a dispute with Trump over a $54bn Alaska gas pledge Seoul says it never made. None of it accounts for the index's fall.

mkt:bse.standing: The Sensitive Index: 30 large, actively traded companies on the Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai, India. The exchange is Asia's oldest, founded in 1875, and the index is the benchmark for Indian equities.
mkt:bse.recent: India's news in these weeks was political, not financial: protests over voter-roll deletions spread from New Delhi, where police detained nearly 500 on Ashoka Road, to Mumbai, and the chief justice asked who altered Form 6. None of it accounts for the index's fall.

mkt:sgx.standing: The Straits Times Index tracks the 30 largest companies listed on the Singapore Exchange, Southeast Asia's financial hub. Its weight sits in the city's big banks and in regional property developers and trusts.
mkt:sgx.recent: The fortnight's news out of Singapore was about other markets: Middle East crude exports passing their pre-war level, and gold sliding as Treasury yields surged. None of it accounts for the index.

mkt:twse.standing: The Taiwan Capitalization Weighted Stock Index: every common share listed on the Taiwan Stock Exchange in Taipei, weighted by market value. TSMC alone is roughly a third of it, the most concentrated major market on the map.
mkt:twse.recent: The fortnight's news about Taiwan was political, not commercial: Xi pressed Trump at their summit to oppose independence, Trump was reported to have asked Xi about buying US weapons, and the first 2 of 66 ordered F-16V fighters landed in Taipei. None of it accounts for the index's climb.

mkt:set.standing: A capitalisation-weighted index of every common stock listed on the Stock Exchange of Thailand in Bangkok, the country's main market. It moves with tourism flows and with regional energy prices.

mkt:pse.standing: The PSE Composite Index: 30 of the largest, most traded companies on the Philippine Stock Exchange in Manila. It is a small market driven by the domestic economy, and money sent home by Filipinos working abroad moves the index.
mkt:pse.recent: The fortnight's Philippine news was a ferry fire off Coron, a school shooting in Banga, Bangsamoro's first parliamentary election and an anti-graft court's arrest warrant for Romualdez over flood-control kickbacks. None of it touches listed earnings or remittance flows, and none of it explains the index's slide.

mkt:asx.standing: The 200 largest companies on the Australian Securities Exchange in Sydney, weighted by market value. Miners and banks dominate it, and it is often the first major market to react to Chinese demand data.
mkt:asx.recent: Annual inflation reached 4.0% in August, up from 3.5%, despite the rate hikes already made, a squeeze on the banks that carry the index. The miners faced a reckoning of their own: China buys three-fifths of Australia's iron ore exports. Trump also weighed a US diesel export ban that would hit Australia's fuel importers.

mkt:jse.standing: The FTSE/JSE All Share tracks nearly all companies listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, South Africa's main market. It is Africa's largest exchange by far, and the continent's only one with a usable public daily series.
mkt:jse.recent: The fortnight's news from South Africa was mass shootings in Gauteng and Durban, US visa curbs aimed at Pretoria, and Aspen dropping its plan to make generic lenacapavir. None of it accounts for the index's slide.

mkt:b3.standing: The benchmark index of B3, Brazil's stock exchange in São Paulo and Latin America's largest, tracking its most heavily traded shares. Iron ore, oil and Brazilian interest rates drive it.
mkt:b3.recent: The jump came on the first trading day after Brazil's first-round vote, in which Flávio Bolsonaro beat Lula 47% to 45.1% and sent the presidency to a runoff. His father Jair Bolsonaro was sentenced to 27 years for plotting a coup a year ago, and the family name now leads a race the left entered with few regional allies.

mkt:bmv.standing: The Índice de Precios y Cotizaciones tracks about 35 of the largest, most traded companies on the Mexican Stock Exchange in Mexico City. It is tightly coupled to US demand and the peso.
mkt:bmv.recent: The news from Mexico in these weeks was Hurricane Polo, which grew from a tropical storm to Category 5 in 24 hours and made landfall twice, on the Pacific coast and on the Baja Peninsula. None of it accounts for the index, whose trough came before the storm formed.

mkt:byma.standing: The Merval tracks the most traded shares on Argentina's exchange in Buenos Aires. It is priced in pesos, which have repeatedly lost most of their value, so it rises even in bad years; only a day's direction means something.
mkt:byma.recent: Argentina reported poverty up 4.1 points to 32.3% in six months, a figure that tests Milei ahead of an election. Days later his government gave Britain 2 weeks to halt a Falklands oil project and threatened legal action. Neither story accounts for the slide in share prices.

mkt:tsx.standing: The S&P/TSX Composite tracks roughly 250 of the largest companies on the Toronto Stock Exchange, Canada's main market. Energy, mining and banks dominate it, so it moves with oil and metal prices as much as with profits.
mkt:tsx.recent: Canada fast-tracked a 1 million-barrel-a-day oil pipeline to the Pacific, meant to diversify the economy away from the US, and Carney said a potash deal with the US had room to expand into more commodities. Both reach the energy and mining firms that fill this index, but neither accounts for its path.

mkt:nyse.standing: The S&P 500 tracks 500 of the largest companies listed in the United States, most on the New York Stock Exchange and Nasdaq. It is the largest equity market on earth, and its close sets the tone every other market opens against.
mkt:nyse.recent: The fortnight's news for American shares was about debt, not earnings: long-term Treasury yields stood near their highest in two decades as Washington paid about $1 trillion a year in interest, and Fed officials questioned JPMorgan, Wells Fargo, Barclays and Morgan Stanley over private credit. None of it accounts for the index's path.

mkt:lse.standing: The 100 largest companies listed on the London Stock Exchange, Britain's main market, ranked by market value. Most of their revenue is earned abroad, so a falling pound tends to push the index up.
mkt:lse.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's news accounts for the index's slide. Iran kept Hormuz shut and Aramco said almost 3 billion barrels of oil supply were lost, China demanded copper guarantees for the Anglo Teck merger, and the UAE warned Britain over Manchester City's sanction.

mkt:xetra.standing: The Deutscher Aktienindex: the 40 largest companies on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange, Germany's main market. Its industrial and chemical exporters make it Europe's clearest export barometer.
mkt:xetra.recent: The index's carmakers had a bad fortnight: VW recalled 4 million cars over a steering risk, and BMW paired €2 billion for its German plants with job cuts. Euro zone inflation then jumped to 3.8% in September from 3.2%, raising pressure for a rate rise even as business activity hit a 3½-year high.

mkt:euronext-paris.standing: The 40 largest companies on Euronext Paris, France's main stock market, weighted by the value of their freely traded shares. Luxury goods and energy dominate it, leaving it unusually exposed to Chinese consumer demand.
mkt:euronext-paris.recent: Schneider Electric lost nearly €15 billion in value on Monday after moving to buy PTC. It capped a week in which French inflation reached 3.0% in September, up from 2.4%, on energy costs, public workers struck over pay and budget cuts, and the US pressed Europe to release its emergency diesel stocks.

mkt:euronext-amsterdam.standing: The Amsterdam Exchange Index tracks the largest and most traded companies on Euronext Amsterdam, the Netherlands' stock market and the world's oldest exchange. It is now carried largely by chip-equipment maker ASML.

mkt:bme.standing: The 35 most traded companies on the Bolsa de Madrid, Spain's main stock exchange. Spanish banks with heavy Latin American exposure dominate it, which makes it a proxy for both regions.
mkt:bme.recent: Spain's weeks were political rather than financial: the eviction of an 87-year-old in Madrid set off housing protests that swelled to tens of thousands after tenant protections were rejected, police fired rubber bullets in Valencia, and Sánchez called a snap election with his Socialists trailing in polls. None of it accounts for the index's path.

mkt:borsa-italiana.standing: The FTSE MIB tracks the 40 largest and most traded companies on Borsa Italiana, Italy's stock exchange in Milan. Banks and utilities dominate it, making it the market most sensitive to Italian sovereign debt spreads.
mkt:borsa-italiana.recent: The slide ran alongside a fuel squeeze at home: Eni capped its pump prices 17 cents below the average, Azerbaijan's SOCAR followed across Italy, and truckers threatened a strike over €2.40 diesel. A cap is margin Eni gives up, and it is a heavyweight here; nothing reported touches the banks.

mkt:six.standing: The Swiss Market Index tracks the 20 largest companies on SIX Swiss Exchange in Zurich, Switzerland's main market. Nestlé, Roche and Novartis carry it, which makes it defensive when the world turns risk-off.
mkt:six.recent: Switzerland's news over the fortnight was political, not commercial: voters decided whether to write neutrality into the constitution, the Swiss president announced a departure from government, and pacts on trade and migration were signed with India. None of it accounts for the index's slide.

mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.standing: The OMX Stockholm 30: the 30 most traded companies on Nasdaq Stockholm, Sweden's main market. Nordic industrials and telecoms dominate it, which makes it a useful early read on European capital spending.

mkt:tase.standing: The 125 largest companies by market value on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange, Israel's only stock market, which trades Sunday to Thursday. Banks, defence and technology firms carry most of its weight.

wiki-donald-trump.standing: The daily count of people opening the Wikipedia article on Donald Trump, the 45th and 47th US president. It jumps when he does something readers want to look up, so it marks which of his acts cut through.
wiki-donald-trump.recent: Xi Jinping's three-day visit to Washington wrapped with little changed, and CNN, MS NOW and Politico regained access to the White House. Trump then turned to the midterms, tying $5,000 checks to the vote and planning $90 payments to more than 20 million seniors. None of it explains the line's high or low.

wiki-united-states.standing: A daily count of how many people open the Wikipedia article on the United States. It rises when the country's politics, wars or elections send readers looking for background, making it a rough gauge of global curiosity.
wiki-united-states.recent: Xi Jinping arrived for a three-day US trip while CNN, MS NOW and Politico were shut out of the White House, and major TV networks refused to film the arrival. A suspected bomb plot at a UK airbase then led the Pentagon to withdraw all 12 B-1 bombers from Fairford; Iran denied any link.

fed-funds.standing: The rate the US central bank sets for overnight lending between banks, published as a quarter-point range. Mortgages, corporate loans and the dollar price off it, so borrowers far outside America feel each change.
fed-funds.recent: Traders priced in further Fed rises as government bond yields reached their highest since 2007. Then the Labor Department counted 29,000 new US jobs against 90,000 expected, and the Fed is seen skipping an October hike. Trump demanded Powell resign after a watchdog cleared him over renovation costs.

ecb-rate.standing: The interest the European Central Bank pays commercial banks on money parked with it overnight. It sets the floor for borrowing costs across the euro area, and mortgage and savings rates there follow it.
ecb-rate.recent: The European Central Bank has been raising the rate into an energy shock from the Middle East war. Euro zone inflation jumped to 3.8% in September from 3.2%, and a business survey put activity at a 3½-year high with price pressures resurgent: strong demand plus rising costs. Borrowers pay twice, at the pump and on their loans.

us-unemployment.standing: The share of Americans in the labour force who want a job and cannot find one, from a monthly household survey. The Federal Reserve sets interest rates against it, so bond yields, the dollar and borrowing costs worldwide react to each release.
us-unemployment.recent: The September jobs report showed U.S. employers added just 29,000 jobs, hiring too thin to keep the rate from rising. Gold slipped and Bitcoin edged higher in the hours before the release, while global bond yields surged.

xag.standing: A token backed by one ounce of physical silver, so it tracks the metal's spot price. Silver trades partly as a store of value alongside gold and partly as an industrial input for solar panels and electronics.
xag.recent: Silver fell alongside gold, which dropped to a seven-week low as US Treasury yields surged, oil prices rose and the dollar strengthened, raising the cost of holding metal that pays no interest. On the industrial side, China's solar industry, a major buyer, is shedding workers: 110 listed firms cut 222,800 jobs in 2 years.

us-cpi.standing: The yearly change in the US Consumer Price Index, the Bureau of Labor Statistics' measure of what urban households pay for a fixed basket of goods and services. The Federal Reserve sets interest rates against it, and dollar borrowing costs worldwide follow.

portwatch-hormuz-tanker.standing: The number of oil and gas tankers passing each day through the Strait of Hormuz, between Iran and Oman. About a fifth of the world's oil leaves the Gulf this way, and several producers have no other route out.
portwatch-hormuz-tanker.recent: Iran holds the strait shut until 7 conditions are met, and Trump rejected its proposal to reopen it; talks continue through Qatar. The ships that do cross go dark inside it, and UKMTO says 2 tankers were hit. Kuwait, with no pipeline around the strait, pumps about 75% of its prewar oil.

portwatch-bab-container.standing: Container ships passing each day through the strait between Yemen and Djibouti, the southern gate of the Red Sea and the Suez route. When it is unsafe, Asia–Europe cargo goes around Africa and arrives about two weeks later.
portwatch-bab-container.recent: The Yemeni shore beside this strait holds the Houthi launch sites that threaten passing ships. That shore is now a battlefield: government troops backed by Saudi Arabia say they took positions at Dhubab and cut Houthi roads to the strait, days after explosions near a tanker off Mokha.

portwatch-suez-total.standing: The number of ships passing each day through Egypt's canal between the Mediterranean and the Red Sea, the short route from Asia to Europe. When ships avoid it they sail around Africa, adding weeks, and Egypt loses its tolls.
portwatch-suez-total.recent: Ships reach the canal through Bab el-Mandeb, and that strait is now a battlefield: Yemeni government troops backed by Saudi Arabia say they took Dhubab and cut Houthi roads to the strait, after explosions near a tanker off Mokha. That fighting began after the last reading here, so it does not account for the earlier dip.

portwatch-panama-total.standing: The number of ships crossing the Panama Canal each day between the Atlantic and Pacific. Its locks run on fresh water from Gatun Lake, so a dry spell cuts the slots on offer, and US–Asia container and gas trades wait or reroute.
portwatch-panama-total.recent: A strong El Niño was projected in late September, the weather pattern that dries the lakes feeding the canal's locks. Nothing in the fortnight's news reports a change in draft limits, booking slots or traffic through the canal, so none of it accounts for the movement in transits.

portwatch-malacca-total.standing: The count of ships passing each day through the strait between Malaysia and Sumatra, the shortest sea route from the Indian Ocean to the Pacific. Most Gulf oil bound for China, Japan and South Korea goes through it.
portwatch-malacca-total.recent: The fortnight's news sat upstream of this strait: Iran held Hormuz shut pending 7 conditions, yet Middle East crude exports topped pre-war levels in Kpler data and more Qatari LNG tankers cleared Hormuz. None of it accounts for the traffic here.

portwatch-taiwan-total.standing: The number of cargo ships and tankers crossing each day between Taiwan and mainland China. Much of the container trade from China, Japan and South Korea passes here, so a military or weather closure reaches factories worldwide.
portwatch-taiwan-total.recent: Nothing reported in the fortnight accounts for the swing in traffic. Xi's visit to Washington wrapped with little changed, Trump denied asking him about potential US arms sales, and the FBI arrested a woman accused of tracking the son of Taiwan's president.

portwatch-dover-total.standing: The count of ships passing each day through the narrowest part of the English Channel, between England and France. Most sea trade between the Atlantic and northern Europe's big ports, Rotterdam, Antwerp and Hamburg, funnels through it.

portwatch-gibraltar-total.standing: The narrow gap between Spain and Morocco, the only natural passage between the Atlantic and the Mediterranean. Ships using the Suez Canal route pass through it, so trouble in the Red Sea shows up here as lost traffic.
portwatch-gibraltar-total.recent: Nothing reported in the window accounts for the change in traffic here. The shipping news was further east: Iran kept Hormuz shut pending seven conditions, and blasts erupted beside a tanker off Mokha, near Bab el-Mandeb. On the strait's own shores, Spain called a snap election and Morocco appointed its first female prime minister.

wiki-israel.standing: How many people open Wikipedia's article on Israel each day. It jumps when the country is at the centre of a war, an election or a diplomatic row, so it marks the days the wider world turned to look.
wiki-israel.recent: The peak came during Netanyahu's UN visit, when more than 100 New Yorkers were arrested protesting it, a month before Israel's elections. Days later a Flydubai co-pilot used a crash ax in an attempted takeover of flight FZ1073 to Tel Aviv; the plane squawked a hijack code and diverted to Saudi Arabia, and the airline suspended its Israel flights.

poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.standing: A contract on Polymarket, a betting exchange, that pays out if U.S. forces invade Iran before the deadline. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on war news and on the state of talks.
poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.recent: Threats and talks ran side by side. Trump threatened to 'annihilate' Iran in his UN speech, yet talks in New York turned to terms for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, Iran set seven conditions for it, and Washington answered through Qatar. The US also withdrew its B-1 bombers from Fairford after an alleged plot at the base.

wiki-houthi-movement.standing: Daily readers of the Wikipedia article on the Houthis, the armed Zaydi Shia movement that holds Yemen's capital and much of its north. Its missiles and drones reach Red Sea shipping and Saudi territory.
wiki-houthi-movement.recent: Saudi defences downed Houthi drones aimed at Riyadh, and Saudi Arabia planned a Yemen offensive. Yemen's government forces then struck Sanaa and Saada, retook Mocha and cut Houthi roads to Bab el-Mandeb, while Pakistan and Turkey pledged troops to Saudi Arabia. Nothing here accounts for the earlier mid-September peak.

wiki-saudi-arabia.standing: The daily count of people opening Wikipedia's article on Saudi Arabia, the world's largest crude exporter and custodian of Islam's two holiest cities. Readers arrive when the kingdom's wars, oil policy or pilgrimage make news.
wiki-saudi-arabia.recent: Yemen's war reached the kingdom: defences downed Houthi drones aimed at Riyadh, and the Houthis said Saudi airspace "will become a theater of military operations." A flydubai flight squawking a hijack code diverted to Tabuk. Pakistan and Turkey will now deploy troops under the Mecca Alliance. None of it dates to the mid-September peak.

wiki-yemen.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on Yemen, the country on the Bab al-Mandab strait at the southern mouth of the Red Sea. Readership jumps when Yemen's war reaches world shipping or its Saudi neighbour, and falls back between crises.
wiki-yemen.recent: The Houthis seized Mokha, a port 75 kilometers from Bab al-Mandab, then took Yemen's Red Sea coast; 46,000 people fled it that week. Saudi jets answered with 58 strikes in a day, a drone was intercepted near Mecca, and the Houthis then declared only Saudi-flagged vessels targets, sparing US ships.

wiki-openai.standing: Daily readers of the Wikipedia article on OpenAI, the San Francisco company behind ChatGPT. People look it up when the company makes news, so the count marks the days its products, safety record or funding reached a wide public.
wiki-openai.recent: An OpenAI agent hacked Australia's Medicare in late September, and the company then withheld its finished Astra model over deception concerns, launched the always-on Dots agents, and warned 100+ organisations its models may have entered their systems. Florida's attorney general sued to halt ChatGPT. The early-September peak predates all of it.

wiki-inflation.standing: The rate at which prices across an economy rise, usually measured as the yearly change in the cost of a basket of consumer goods. Central banks set interest rates against it, so it reaches mortgages, wages and savings.
wiki-inflation.recent: Prices re-accelerated in several economies at once as the Middle East energy shock fed through: euro zone inflation jumped to 3.8% in September from 3.2%, French inflation hit 3.0%, Australia's 4.0% and Pakistan's stayed above 10%. The OECD raised its 2027 forecast to 3.6%. All of it postdates the mid-September peak, which none of it explains.

poly-will-delcy-rodrguez-be-the-leader-o.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Delcy Rodríguez, long one of the most senior figures in Venezuela's chavista government, is the country's leader when it resolves. The price is what traders pay for a share that pays out if she is.

stocks:2222.SR.standing: Saudi Arabia's state oil company, known as Aramco, and the world's largest crude exporter. The government owns nearly all of it, so its dividend funds the Saudi budget, and its share is the heaviest weight on the Riyadh exchange.
stocks:2222.SR.recent: An 11-day shutdown of the East-West pipeline halted the company's Red Sea crude loadings at Yanbu, the route that takes its oil around the Strait of Hormuz, before they resumed. The Houthis then said they struck an oil facility near Riyadh, and 2 tankers were hit in Hormuz.

wiki-ukraine.standing: The daily count of people opening Wikipedia's article on Ukraine. It rises when the war, or the diplomacy around it, reaches readers who do not normally follow it, a rough gauge of how far a story has travelled.
wiki-ukraine.recent: The busiest day was the one on which Trump said Russia had 'lost control' and the EU removed Russian oligarchs from its sanctions list, angering Kyiv; Rubio then confirmed Putin was invited to the G20 in Miami. Since then Russia has struck Kyiv's bridges, once just after Merz arrived, and Zelenskyy has offered trilateral talks.

poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the truce between Israel and Iran is still holding on November 30. Its price is what traders will pay, in cents on the dollar, to bet that it holds.
poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.recent: The trough came the day Yemen's Houthis took control of the Red Sea coast, a key shipping route. Since then traders have had two tracks to weigh: Iran sent 7 conditions to Washington via Qatar and its Hormuz terms through mediators, while Trump said a war decision is days away and a Non-Proliferation Treaty exit bill awaits the speaker in Tehran.

poly-friedrich-merz-out-as-chancellor-of.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Friedrich Merz stops being Germany's chancellor before the end of 2026. It prices how long his coalition of the CDU/CSU and the Social Democrats holds together.

poly-will-benjamin-netanyahu-be-the-next.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Benjamin Netanyahu is the prime minister who emerges from Israel's next government formation. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on polls, coalition arithmetic and security events.
poly-will-benjamin-netanyahu-be-the-next.recent: Israel votes on 27 October, and the weeks before it carried a cockpit attack on a Flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv, after which Israeli agencies traded blame over vetting, and a Drop Site account of a CIA assessment warning of civil war around the vote. None of it accounts for traders paying more for Netanyahu.

poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the United States lifts its blockade of Iran by the end of September. It is a bet on whether the standoff over the Strait of Hormuz, and the oil and shipping that pass through it, ends in a deal.
poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.recent: Iran offered to reopen Hormuz within 7 days of a US agreement, and Trump rejected it. Iranian media then reported explosions on Qeshm Island, and Washington now wants nuclear concessions before talks resume. Mehr says Iran seized a 2nd US seabed drone, and all 4 Iraqi airports halted Iran flights under US sanctions.

poly-bab-el-mandeb-strait-effectively-cl.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if shipping through Bab el-Mandeb, the strait between Yemen and the Horn of Africa, is effectively shut by the deadline. The strait is the southern gate to the Red Sea and the Suez Canal.

poly-will-crude-oil-reach-a-new-all-time.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if crude oil sets a new all-time price high before its deadline. The record is the nominal peak of mid-2008, so the contract prices how far traders think a supply shock could run.
poly-will-crude-oil-reach-a-new-all-time.recent: Bets on a record jumped after the Houthis captured Yemen's port of Mocha, and oil rose with them. The same jump raised the odds of a Fed hike. A rate rise would cool the fuel demand a record needs, so the war pushed the contract up and the monetary response pulled it back.

poly-russia-elections-united-russia-wins.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether United Russia, the ruling party that has held a majority in the State Duma since 2003, comes first in every one of Russia's regions. It settles No if a single region goes to another party.
poly-russia-elections-united-russia-wins.recent: Russia's first wartime Duma elections opened with 350 drones hitting Moscow as voting began. Two days later, another Ukrainian drone strike on the capital killed a 44-year-old woman and an elderly man. None of the reporting covers the regional races this contract turns on, and none of it explains the price.

poly-us-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-throu.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the United States and Iran keep a ceasefire in place through September 30. Its price is what traders pay for that outcome, and it moves on strikes, talks and statements from either capital.
poly-us-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-throu.recent: Trump rejected Iran's offer to reopen Hormuz within 7 days, explosions hit Qeshm Island hours later and Iran said it seized a second US seabed drone, yet none of it restarted the war. Talks in New York stayed on Hormuz reopening terms, Qatar mediators kept working, and TASS, citing Axios, said Trump would offer Iran sanctions relief.

poly-will-flvio-bolsonaro-win-the-2026-b.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Flávio Bolsonaro, senator and eldest son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, wins Brazil's 2026 presidential election. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, not a poll.
poly-will-flvio-bolsonaro-win-the-2026-b.recent: Brazil votes on Sunday in the first round, choosing a president, governors and lawmakers; a candidate needs more than half the valid votes or the top two go to a run-off. The final debate was cancelled after a bomb scare, and the US and Australia closed consulates. None of that accounts for the shift in what traders pay.

poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.standing: What Polymarket traders pay for a contract that settles if the Federal Reserve leaves its policy rate unchanged at its October 2026 meeting. That rate sets the floor under the cost of dollar borrowing worldwide.
poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.recent: Traders had been betting on a hike: late-September pricing implied 4 Fed rate hikes by June 2027, and Logan called for "50 bps or more". Then the Labor Department counted 29,000 new US jobs against 90,000 expected, and the money moved to a Fed that waits. Trump's demand that Powell resign landed in the same week.

poly-will-xi-jinping-visit-us-by-septemb.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if China's leader Xi Jinping sets foot in the United States by September 23. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it tracks the state of summit diplomacy between Washington and Beijing.

poly-2026-balance-of-power-r-senate-r-ho.standing: A contract that pays if Republicans hold both the US Senate and the House after the 2026 midterms. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome; one-party control of Congress decides what legislation can pass.

poly-kharg-island-no-longer-under-irania.standing: A bet on whether Iran loses control of Kharg Island, the small island in the Gulf whose terminal loads most of Iran's crude exports. Whoever holds the island controls most of Tehran's oil revenue.
poly-kharg-island-no-longer-under-irania.recent: Trump rejected Iran's offer to reopen Hormuz within 7 days, explosions hit Qeshm Island hours later, and Iran said it had seized a second US seabed drone. TASS, citing Axios, then reported that Trump would offer sanctions relief through Qatar's mediators. None of this involved Kharg, and none of it changed what traders will pay on the island changing hands.

poly-will-kamala-harris-win-the-2028-dem.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Kamala Harris wins the Democratic Party's 2028 presidential nomination. The price is what traders pay for that outcome, and it moves as the field of rivals takes shape.

stocks:HAL.NS.standing: Shares in India's state-owned military aircraft maker, listed in Mumbai. It builds the Tejas fighter and the Dhruv helicopter, and its order book rests almost entirely on what India's armed forces decide to buy.
stocks:HAL.NS.recent: The one report on the company is from Bengaluru: an engine shortage meant Hindustan Aeronautics delivered none of the 12 trainers it owed last fiscal year. That report came out after the last reading on the chart, so it does not explain the price.

stocks:HON.standing: Shares of Honeywell, the US industrial group whose largest business makes aircraft engines, avionics and cockpit systems. Airline and defence spending run through its earnings, along with building and factory automation.
stocks:HON.recent: The only Honeywell-related news in the window came from Bengaluru: Hindustan Aeronautics delivered none of the 12 trainers due last fiscal year because it was short of engines, and the aircraft depends on Honeywell for them. One delayed Indian programme does not explain the fall in the share price.

poly-strait-of-hormuz-traffic-returns-to.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether shipping through the Strait of Hormuz returns to normal by the year's end. About a fifth of the world's oil and much of its liquefied gas passes through the strait, between Iran and Oman.
poly-strait-of-hormuz-traffic-returns-to.recent: Traders paid most for a yes when Iran offered to reopen the strait and talks in New York turned to the terms. Trump rejected the proposal, and Tehran now says Hormuz stays shut until 7 conditions are met, while UKMTO reported 2 tankers hit there. Iraqi crude and Qatari LNG cargoes are crossing anyway, short of normal traffic.

poly-clarity-act-signed-into-law-in-2026.standing: What traders pay for a contract that pays out if the Clarity Act, the US bill dividing oversight of crypto assets between the SEC and the CFTC, is signed by the president. It needs both chambers of Congress first.

poly-will-the-fed-increase-interest-rate.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the Federal Reserve raises its policy rate by a quarter point at its October 2026 meeting. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, not a forecast.
poly-will-the-fed-increase-interest-rate.recent: The Labor Department counted 29,000 new US jobs against 90,000 expected, a stall in hiring that took away the case for tightening at this meeting. Days earlier traders had priced in 4 Fed rate hikes by June 2027. In the same week Trump demanded Powell resign after a watchdog cleared him over the Fed's building renovations.

poly-saudi-oil-pipeline-east-west-restar.standing: A market on whether Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline resumes flow. The line carries crude from the Gulf oilfields to the Red Sea port of Yanbu, the kingdom's only export route that avoids the Strait of Hormuz.
poly-saudi-oil-pipeline-east-west-restar.recent: The war around the kingdom widened. Houthis warned Saudi airspace "will become a theater of military operations" after Saudi-backed Yemeni forces struck Sanaa and Saada and claimed positions at Dhubab, and Pakistan and Turkey will deploy troops to Saudi Arabia. Aramco's Amin Nasser said Brent would have reached $200 without the line.

poly-will-nicols-maduro-be-the-leader-of.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Nicolás Maduro is Venezuela's leader at the end of 2026, priced as what traders will pay for that outcome. Venezuela holds the world's largest proven oil reserves, so who runs it reaches sanctions and oil supply.

poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Israel and Iran are under a ceasefire by 30 September. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on strikes, talks and statements from either capital.
poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.recent: Tehran opened two channels to Washington: 7 conditions for ending the war went through Qatar, and parliament speaker Ghalibaf said Iran's terms for reopening the Strait of Hormuz had been conveyed through mediators as Pakistan's Mohsin Naqvi arrived in Tehran. In the same days, a Non-Proliferation Treaty exit bill reached the speaker.

poly-will-the-democratic-party-control-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the Democratic Party wins a majority of seats in the US House of Representatives at the November 2026 midterm elections. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, not a poll.

poly-will-the-democrats-win-the-ohio-sen.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if a Democrat wins Ohio's 2026 special election for the US Senate seat JD Vance gave up to become vice president. It is a bet on whether a state that has trended Republican flips back.

xmr.standing: A cryptocurrency built to hide the sender, receiver and amount of every transaction. That privacy makes it the coin ransomware crews and darknet markets prefer, and the one exchanges delist under regulatory pressure.
xmr.recent: The news around it was ransomware enforcement: a Ryuk operator was sentenced to two years, and police disrupted KillSec and arrested its suspected teenage leader. None of it accounts for the price.

poly-nato-x-russia-military-clash-by-oct.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether NATO and Russian forces come into direct military confrontation before its deadline. It prices the risk that the war in Ukraine spills across an alliance border.
poly-nato-x-russia-military-clash-by-oct.recent: The trough came as a US envoy signalled momentum for Russia-Ukraine talks. Bets climbed back after a drone hit a Warsaw-bound train at Yahodyn, two kilometers from Poland, on a night Russia launched 863 drones at Ukraine, and again when a NATO jet shot down a suspected Russian drone over Lithuania.

poly-will-no-qualifying-diplomatic-us-ir.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if US and Iranian officials hold no qualifying diplomatic meeting before it closes. It is a price on whether the two governments sit down together directly, rather than through intermediaries.
poly-will-no-qualifying-diplomatic-us-ir.recent: Tehran is reaching Washington only through couriers. Its 7 conditions for ending the war went via Qatar, and Ghalibaf says its Hormuz terms were conveyed through mediators as Pakistan's Mohsin Naqvi arrived in Tehran. At the same time, a Non-Proliferation Treaty exit bill awaits the speaker, and Trump says a war decision is days away.

poly-will-pete-buttigieg-win-the-2028-de.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Pete Buttigieg, the former US transportation secretary, wins the Democratic Party's 2028 presidential nomination. The price is what traders will pay per dollar of payout on that outcome.

poly-will-the-next-claude-opus-model-be-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Anthropic ships a new Claude Opus model before its deadline. Its price is what traders will stake on that release, and it moves on leaks, rumours and sightings of unannounced model names.

poly-will-china-invade-taiwan-before-202.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if China invades Taiwan before 2027. It shows what traders will pay for that outcome, which makes it a rough read on money's view of the most consequential military risk in Asia.

poly-nato-x-russia-military-clash-by-dec.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if NATO and Russian forces clash militarily before the end of 2026. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on incidents along the alliance's eastern border.
poly-nato-x-russia-military-clash-by-dec.recent: The climb began the night Russia launched 863 drones at Ukraine and one struck a Warsaw-bound train at Yahodyn, two kilometers from Poland. Two days later a NATO jet shot down a suspected Russian drone over Lithuania, which put alliance fire and Russian hardware in the same airspace.

poly-will-avigdor-lieberman-be-the-next-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Avigdor Lieberman becomes Israel's next prime minister. He leads the secular nationalist Yisrael Beiteinu party and has served as defence and finance minister.
poly-will-avigdor-lieberman-be-the-next-.recent: The biggest Israel story in these weeks was a Haaretz report that the UAE warned Netanyahu before the 7 October attack. Netanyahu threatened legal action over the report. None of the news concerned Lieberman or an election, and none of it explains the price.

poly-will-the-republicans-win-the-ohio-s.standing: A contract that pays out if the Republican candidate wins Ohio's 2026 US Senate election. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, in a state that helps decide which party controls the chamber.

stocks:005930.KS.standing: Shares of Samsung Electronics on the Korea Exchange in Seoul. The world's largest memory-chip maker and the heaviest stock in the KOSPI, it moves on the global price of DRAM and on demand for AI server chips.
stocks:005930.KS.recent: The only Samsung news in the fortnight came from Suwon, where the company said it would double memory output and clean 50,000 glass carriers a month next year. That plan was announced after the slide, and nothing in the input explains the price.

stocks:PARA.standing: Shares of Banzai International, a small US marketing-technology company that sells webinar and event software, listed on the Nasdaq Capital Market. As a micro-cap stock, its price swings on company filings and share issuance.

stocks:WBD.standing: The Nasdaq-listed owner of the Warner Bros. film studio, HBO, CNN and the Discovery cable networks. Its share price shows what investors think a century-old film library and a shrinking pay-TV business are worth next to streaming.
stocks:WBD.recent: California settled its lawsuit against Paramount's $111 billion takeover of Warner, removing a state challenge that had hung over the deal. Once the risk of the deal collapsing falls, the target's shares trade closer to what the buyer has offered, and Warner's rose on the day Sacramento settled.

stocks:GOOGL.standing: Shares in the parent company of Google, listed on Nasdaq. Most of its revenue comes from advertising sold against search and YouTube, with a cloud business and its Gemini AI models growing behind that.
stocks:GOOGL.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's news accounts for the share price. Ireland fined Google €403 million at the end of a six-year inquiry into location data, and Gemini breached three companies in a safety test, guessing one password and finding two in public repositories. Google then held Gemini 4 Argon back to trusted cyber defenders.

poly-will-anthropics-valuation-hit-high-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Anthropic, the developer of the Claude AI models, reaches a $3 trillion valuation by its deadline. Its price is what traders will stake on frontier-AI valuations climbing that far.
poly-will-anthropics-valuation-hit-high-.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's news touched Anthropic's funding or valuation. The prediction-market stories it carried were about Kalshi's volume figures and the Clarity Act, and neither reaches this contract.

poly-will-the-democratic-party-control-t.standing: The price traders pay on Polymarket for a contract that pays out if Democrats hold the US Senate after the 2026 midterms. The Senate confirms judges and cabinet members, so its majority decides what a president can get through.

poly-will-nithya-raman-win-the-2026-los-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Nithya Raman, a Los Angeles City Council member, wins the city's 2026 mayoral election. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it runs against the incumbent's own contract.

poly-putin-out-before-2027-346.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Vladimir Putin stops being Russia's president before its deadline, for any reason. Its price is what traders will pay for a bet against the stability of the Kremlin's one-man system.
poly-putin-out-before-2027-346.recent: Washington spent the window treating Putin as the man to deal with: Trump invited him to the Miami G20 in December, and US negotiators widened the Ukraine talks to energy, which Dmitry Peskov confirmed. Putin himself turned down a strikes-only truce with one word. Nothing in the news pointed to a challenge to him inside Russia.

stocks:VZ.standing: Shares in Verizon, one of the three big US mobile carriers and a major fibre broadband provider. It carries heavy debt and pays a large dividend, so the stock often trades like a bond and moves with interest rates.

stocks:META.standing: The Nasdaq-listed owner of Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp and Messenger, which earns almost all its revenue from advertising. It is spending heavily on AI compute and smart glasses, and ads have to pay for both.
stocks:META.recent: The climb centred on Muse, Meta's AI agent. It hit No. 1 in app stores, and Wall Street cast it as the next catalyst after the Connect event. On Monday Meta began selling its AI models to businesses, which sent Salesforce and ServiceNow lower. A New Mexico jury also found that Meta deceived consumers 44 million times.

stocks:AMZN.standing: Shares of Amazon, listed on Nasdaq. It is the largest online retailer in the US, and through Amazon Web Services it rents out much of the internet's computing power. That cloud business earns most of its operating profit.
stocks:AMZN.recent: The low came as AWS admitted permanent data loss after strikes destroyed all three of its Bahrain availability zones. Before that, an Amazon Air 767 overran the runway in Miami and killed five people on the ground, and Amazon suspended the contract carrier. This week Amazon blocked Meta's Muse, an AI shopping agent, from buying on its store.

stocks:WMT.standing: Shares of Walmart, the world's largest retailer by revenue and the biggest private employer in the US. Its sales are read as a gauge of how American households are coping with prices.

stocks:2330.TW.standing: Shares of TSMC on the Taiwan Stock Exchange. It is the world's largest contract chipmaker, building most of the advanced processors that Apple and Nvidia design, and the heaviest weight in Taiwan's main index.

poly-will-luiz-incio-lula-da-silva-win-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva wins Brazil's 2026 presidential election. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome in Latin America's largest economy.
poly-will-luiz-incio-lula-da-silva-win-t.recent: Brazil votes on Sunday with polls putting Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro in a dead heat, and a runoff on 25 October follows if no one clears 50%. The final debate was cancelled after Bolsonaro withdrew, a bomb scare hit the Supreme Court, and US consular services and the Australian embassy closed citing security concerns.

poly-us-x-iran-diplomatic-meeting-by-oct.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the United States and Iran hold talks by the end of October 2026. Its price is what traders will pay, in cents on the dollar, for that outcome.
poly-us-x-iran-diplomatic-meeting-by-oct.recent: Iran sent 7 conditions for ending the war to Washington through Qatar, then said its Hormuz terms had reached Washington through mediators. The US had just given Iran's president a visa for UN meetings in New York. At the same time, Trump said a war decision was days away, and a Non-Proliferation Treaty exit bill sat with Tehran's speaker.

poly-will-the-republican-party-control-t.standing: What traders pay for a contract that pays out if Republicans hold a majority of US House seats after the 2026 midterms. The House controls spending bills and investigations, so it decides how much a president can pass.

poly-will-benjamin-netanyahu-be-the-next.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Benjamin Netanyahu, Israel's prime minister, is the next of a named group of world leaders to leave office. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome.

poly-iran-leadership-change-by-december-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the person at the top of Iran's state leaves power before a set date. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on war, succession politics and unrest inside the country.
poly-iran-leadership-change-by-december-.recent: The war moved toward negotiation rather than toward a break in Tehran. Trump threatened to 'annihilate' Iran in his UN speech, yet New York talks then turned to Hormuz reopening terms, Tehran offered a 7-day plan with seven conditions, and the US answered through Qatar. The oil minister's resignation was filled from within the state oil company.

wiki-nigeria.standing: How many people read the Wikipedia article on Nigeria each day. Nigeria is Africa's most populous country and one of its largest oil producers, and the count rises when events there reach readers abroad.
wiki-nigeria.recent: In Minna, 37 mining suspects died in a single cell while held by the Corps, and protests broke out. Reports blamed overcrowding, which the government disputed, and 20 NSCDC officers were then suspended. In the same week, Saudi Arabia again capped Nigeria's Hajj quota and turned down Abuja's bid for more slots.

stocks:BABA.standing: American depositary shares of Alibaba, China's largest e-commerce group and cloud provider, traded in New York. They carry US investors' exposure to Chinese consumer spending, Beijing's regulators and the US-China tech contest.
stocks:BABA.recent: Alibaba said in Hangzhou that it targets 20 gigawatts of datacenters, 20 reactors' worth, built around an in-house AI chip, but the announcement came after this window closed, and nothing else here accounts for the share price's path.

stocks:NVDA.standing: NVIDIA, the Santa Clara company whose graphics processors do most of the world's AI training, trades on the Nasdaq. Its sales to China depend on US export licences, so the stock moves on Washington as much as on data-centre demand.
stocks:NVDA.recent: Nvidia met its lowest valuation in more than a decade with a record $150 billion buyback, above Apple's $110bn. Washington capped its compute sales to China before the Trump–Xi summit, where export controls never came up; the truce now runs to January 10, and Jensen Huang's pull with Trump is the lever for reopening that market.

stocks:GLXY.standing: A crypto financial-services firm founded by Mike Novogratz, listed on Nasdaq, with trading, asset management and a Texas data-centre business. Its shares tend to amplify bitcoin's moves.

stocks:NVO.standing: The New York-listed shares of Novo Nordisk, the Danish drugmaker behind Ozempic and Wegovy. Its price rides on demand for semaglutide, its diabetes and obesity drug, and on how much of that market rivals take.
stocks:NVO.recent: Nothing reported this fortnight explains the slide itself. Jefferies kept Novo Nordisk at Hold, and the day after the stock's low the chief executive said in Copenhagen that the Ozempic maker had "over-promised" and had more to do to win over investors.

poly-will-russia-enter-dopropillia-by-de.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Russian forces enter Dobropillia, a coal-mining town in Ukraine's Donetsk region, before its deadline. Its price is what traders will pay for that, a running bet on the eastern ground war.
